question: Who is responsible for hoisting the flag on Independence Day?
solution:
The correct answer is __**The Prime Minister of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Prime Minister of India is responsible for hoisting the national flag at the Red Fort in Delhi on Independence Day, which is celebrated on August 15th every year.
 
• This tradition started with the first Prime Minister of India, Jawaharlal Nehru, who hoisted the flag on August 15, 1947, marking India’s independence from British rule.
 
• The Prime Minister's Independence Day speech from the Red Fort outlines the government's policies and achievements and highlights future plans for the nation's development.
 
• During the flag hoisting ceremony, the Prime Minister is accompanied by various dignitaries, including senior government officials, military personnel, and school children.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Independence Day**

 
 
• It is a national holiday in India commemorating the nation's independence from the United Kingdom on August 15, 1947.
 
• On this day, the Indian Independence Act 1947, which transferred legislative sovereignty to the Indian Constituent Assembly, came into effect.
 
• The day is marked by flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, and cultural events across the country.
 
 
 
• **Red Fort**
 
 
• The Red Fort, located in Delhi, is a historic fort that served as the main residence of the Mughal emperors for nearly 200 years until 1857.
 
• It is the site from which the Prime Minister of India addresses the nation on Independence Day.
 
• The fort was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2007.
 
 
 
• **Flag Hoisting**
 
 
• Flag hoisting on Independence Day symbolizes the freedom and sovereignty of the nation.
 
• It is a ceremonial practice that involves the raising of the national flag on a pole or mast.
 
• The hoisting is accompanied by the national anthem and a salute by the armed forces.
 
 
 
• **National Flag**
 
 
• The national flag of India, also known as the Tiranga, consists of three horizontal stripes of saffron, white, and green, with a blue Ashoka Chakra in the center.
 
• It was adopted on July 22, 1947, and its design is based on the Swaraj flag of the Indian National Congress.
 
• The flag symbolizes courage and sacrifice (saffron), peace and truth (white), and faith and chivalry (green).
